h1:
Where to Stay in Lamphun?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Lamphun hotels across every budget — a garden resort with kids' pools in Pa Sak, a hostel in a restored teak house in the old town, a brand-new resort with a big pool in Wiang Yong, down to a from-฿500 garden resort in Pa Sang. Covering the main areas: the old town around Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, the Wiang Yong–Pa Sak fringe, and the outlying districts. From roughly ฿500–1,050/night.
heroStats: 🛕 3 key areas (Old Town·Wiang Yong-Pa Sak·Outlying districts)
introH2: 🛕 Why does choosing the right area in Lamphun matter?
introHtml: Lamphun is a compact little city you can drive around in one loop, but where you stay still shapes the style of your trip. The old town (around Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, the walking street and the old city wall) is what people who want to walk to temples, browse the market and soak up the old town slowly look for first — you can walk to the temple and markets, but parking is limited. The Wiang Yong–Pa Sak fringe is where the hotels and resorts with swimming pools, bigger rooms and free parking sit, close to Jampha mall, ideal for self-drivers and families — but you can't walk to the temple, you'll drive. And the outlying districts — Pa Sang, Ban Hong and Umong — are quiet garden stays at low prices, best for a stopover or for truly getting away from town. The thing many people miss: Lamphun is much harder for Grab than Chiang Mai, as drivers tend to work the Chiang Mai side — so without your own car, pick a stay you can walk everywhere from in the old town. This guide rounds up 12 Lamphun hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Lamphun has no metro; you get around by car, and it's much harder to get a Grab than in Chiang Mai, since drivers mostly work the Chiang Mai side. Many old-town stays (around Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the walking street) are walkable to the temple, markets and restaurants — best if you don't have a car, though parking is usually tight. Wiang Yong–Pa Sak stays on the fringe are easy in and out of town with free parking, near Jampha mall, but you can't walk to the temple — you'll drive. And almost everything in the outlying districts — Pa Sang, Ban Hong, Umong — needs a private car, as public transport is awkward and dining around the stays is thin. Lamphun sits right next to Chiang Mai — about a 30–40-minute drive to Chiang Mai city or CNX airport — so many people use Lamphun as a quiet base and day-trip into Chiang Mai. The areas in this guide: Old Town — walk to the temple and markets · Wiang Yong–Pa Sak — pools, parking, near the mall · Outlying districts — quiet gardens, low prices.

entries.name: Siri Hotel Lumphun
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wiang Yong · Lamphun · ~5-min drive to Wat Phra That
tags: 🛏️ 34 newly renovated rooms · strong water pressure
entries.storyHtml: Siri Hotel Lumphun takes the top score in this guide at 9.4 from 113 reviews — a 34-room mid-range 3-star that was recently renovated, with genuinely new, clean rooms at a price that's hard to find in Lamphun. It sits in Wiang Yong, about a 5-minute drive from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the city markets. Real guest reviews praise the bright, roomy rooms, firm beds, the satisfyingly strong shower pressure, attentive staff who help above and beyond, and a tasty made-to-order breakfast. The trade-off: it's not in the city centre, and Lamphun is hard for Grab, so without a car getting around isn't easy. Best for self-drivers who want a clean base — sleep well, eat a good breakfast, then head out to the temples.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Reviews note the room type at check-in is occasionally switched, so confirm your bed type (Twin/Double) at the front desk on arrival. Lamphun is hard for Grab, so driving yourself is easiest — parking here is free. Get to breakfast between 07:00–10:00 for the full spread.
pros: Top score 9.4 · cleanliness 9.6 · 34 newly renovated rooms
Bright, roomy rooms, firm beds, strong water pressure
Attentive staff, service above expectations · tasty made-to-order breakfast
24-hour gym, sauna, small pool · free parking
cons: Outside the city centre, hard for Grab — you'll need a car
Small pool, sometimes used for kids' swim classes · limited breakfast menu

entries.name: Look at Home Lamphun
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pa Sak · Lamphun · ~14-min drive to the train station
tags: 🏊 Several outdoor pools + a shallow kids' pool
entries.storyHtml: Look at Home Lamphun is the standout for pools — a garden-home 4-star resort with several outdoor pools and a separate shallow kids' pool, rare among Lamphun stays at this price, scoring 9.2 from 26 reviews. It sits in suburban Pa Sak with a quiet garden-home feel; opened in 2018 and renovated in 2023, so it still looks fresh and clean. Real guest reviews praise the roomy, clean rooms, comfy beds, leafy garden, and a kids' pool shallow enough to let children splash without worry. One reviewer did report being moved to a room that didn't match the booking and having to pay extra, finding the resolution inflexible, and the Pa Sak location needs a car. Best for families bringing kids to swim and for self-drivers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With one report of a mismatched room assignment, confirm your room type, price and guest count clearly when booking. The buffet breakfast is usually an extra ~฿150/person, so check whether it's included. Take the kids to the shallow pool — bring your own swimwear.
pros: Several pools + a kids' pool, rare at this price
Newly built, renovated 2023 · roomy, clean rooms, comfy beds
Quiet, leafy, private garden-home feel
Generous free parking, good for families and drivers
cons: Pa Sak location, away from the old town — needs a car, few restaurants in walking distance
One report of a mismatched room assignment · breakfast charged separately

entries.name: Pickbaan Hostel & Cafe
entries.revCount: Booking 9.0 · 196 reviews (most in the guide) · TripAdvisor 4.6/5

tags: ☕ Specialty coffee cafe on site, owner-barista
🏛️ Walk to the walking street + Wat Phra That
🚲 Free bikes + breakfast in the garden
entries.storyHtml: Pickbaan Hostel & Cafe is the most-reviewed property in this guide — 196 reviews — a restored old teak house in the heart of Lamphun's old town, with a genuine specialty coffee cafe on the ground floor, scoring 9.0 on Booking and 4.6/5 on TripAdvisor (#2 specialty lodging in Lamphun). You can walk to the walking street and Wat Phra That Hariphunchai. Real guest reviews praise the old-town walkability, coffee made by the owner-barista, a made-to-order breakfast that changes almost daily served in the garden, and free bikes for exploring. It is an old wooden house, though — shared bathrooms downstairs, some late-night noise from the cafe, and it's an adults-only stay that doesn't take children. Best for solo travellers or couples who like a stay with character.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For more privacy choose a private room over a dorm, and ask for a room deeper from the cafe if you're a light sleeper. Try at least one coffee at the downstairs cafe. Borrow a bike for a loop around the old city wall — ask the owner for routes.
pros: Most reviews in the guide (196) · 9.0 on Booking · TripAdvisor 4.6/5
Genuine specialty coffee cafe on site, owner-barista
Walk to the walking street and Wat Phra That Hariphunchai
Free bikes · made-to-order garden breakfast · characterful old teak house

entries.name: GRAND PA Hotel & Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wiang Yong · 1 min to Jampha mall · 5 min to Wat Phra That
tags: 🏊 Big pool + Pool Bar · full gym
🛍️ ~1 min to Jampha mall · 5 min to Wat Phra That
entries.addr: 110/1 Lamphun-Doi Ti Rd, Wiang Yong, Mueang Lamphun
entries.storyHtml: GRAND PA Hotel & Resort is a newly opened boutique 4-star with the fullest facilities in this guide — 125 rooms, a big pool with a Pool Bar, a gym, a cafe, a fresh bakery and a minimart, scoring 8.8 from 141 reviews. It sits in Wiang Yong, about a minute from Jampha shopping mall and 5 minutes from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai. Real guest reviews praise the roomy, clean rooms, the big pool, well-equipped gym, and a buffet breakfast many call better than at pricier hotels. The trade-off: it's outside the old town, so no evening temple stroll, and some roadside rooms catch traffic noise. Best for families, self-drivers and groups here for meetings.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The building is near a main road, so if you're a light sleeper ask for an inner or higher-floor room when booking. Get to breakfast early (07:00–10:00) for the full spread. Allow afternoon-evening time to make the most of the pool and Pool Bar.
pros: Fullest facilities here · big pool, Pool Bar · full gym
Very roomy, clean rooms, soft beds (newly opened)
Buffet breakfast better than expected · cafe-bakery on site

entries.name: Loft House Homestay
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Hong · rural Lamphun · ~40-min drive to old town
entries.storyHtml: Loft House Homestay (formerly OYO 659) is a budget homestay scoring a surprising 9.2 — with 9.2 across the board for cleanliness, facilities, location and service, from 18 reviews. It's a roughly 10–11 room stay in Ban Hong, in the southwest of Lamphun. Real guest reviews agree the rooms are cleaner than the price suggests, quiet, with fast Wi-Fi and a 24-hour front desk that's rare at this price, and some rooms have a fridge and small kitchenette. The catch: it's out in the countryside, about 40 minutes from the old town, with no breakfast and no pool, and you'll need your own car. Best for self-drivers and budget travellers stopping over around Ban Hong.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There's no breakfast and few shops nearby, so pick up supplies at a convenience store or local market ahead of time. For longer stays, ask for a room with a fridge/kitchenette to save on food. Late arrivals are fine, but flag a rough ETA.
pros: 9.2 across the board · rooms cleaner than the price suggests
Quiet, restful · fast Wi-Fi

entries.storyHtml: Nornlamphun Boutique Hotel is a modern-loft boutique with rooms larger than the price suggests for a few thousand baht — parquet floors, an airy high-ceilinged lobby, and pet-friendly, which is rare in Lamphun, scoring around 9.0 on Agoda / 8.6 on Booking from 99 reviews, with cleanliness at 9.2. It sits in Mueang Nga, about 2–3 km from the city centre, just 3 minutes from the train station, and 15–20 minutes' drive into Chiang Mai. Real guest reviews praise the roomy, clean, nicely styled loft rooms and the friendly owner. Reviewers note some late-night noise from guests or music, a tea-coffee-corner breakfast with limited choice, and few restaurants nearby. Best for self-drivers, pet owners, and using Lamphun as a two-city base.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, ask for an inner room away from the lobby when booking and pack earplugs. Bringing a pet? Tell the hotel ahead to check the terms and any fee. Few restaurants nearby — plan to drive into town for food.

entries.name: The Grand Jamjuree Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mueang Nga · ~1 km to the city · 2 km to Wat Phra That
tags: 🌳 Cottages around a lake, leafy and quiet

entries.storyHtml: The Grand Jamjuree Resort is a 3-star cottage resort with rooms set around a lake amid leafy grounds — a genuine resort feel rather than a block, rare in a small city like Lamphun, scoring 8.4 from 120 reviews. It sits in Mueang Nga, just about 1 km from the city centre and 2 km from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai. Real guest reviews most love the leafy grounds and the quiet, plus a pool, Panna Spa, free bikes, parking for over 250 cars, and a Thai breakfast. The trade-off: being by a lake, there can be plenty of mosquitoes and insects on some nights, especially in the rainy season, the entrance is hard to find without GPS, and some cottages' furniture shows its age. Best for self-drivers, groups and families who want a resort rather than a block.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The entrance sign is unclear and the lane is deep — set GPS before you arrive. Pack mosquito repellent and pick a room not too close to the lake if insects bother you. Borrow a bike and ride to Wat Phra That (~2 km) in the morning for a nice atmosphere.
pros: Cottages around a lake, leafy and quiet · genuine resort feel
Pool, Panna Spa · free bikes · parking for 250+ cars
~1 km to the city · 2 km to Wat Phra That · tasty Thai breakfast

entries.storyHtml: The First Residence Lamphun is an old-town 3-star city hotel that's all about location — a 0.6 km (10-minute) walk to Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and close to the train station, scoring 8.6 from 7 reviews (location a high 9.0). It's a roughly 30-room hotel in the old town, opened around 2014 and renovated in 2024. Real guest reviews praise the walkable location to the temple and markets, clean rooms with balconies, and the value. The trade-off: reviews mention occasional check-in issues with no one at the desk and being hard to reach by phone, there's no pool and no pets, and reviews are still few. Best for temple visitors, old-town walkers, or anyone arriving by train.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With reports of no one at the desk at times, call or message to confirm your check-in time ahead, especially for late arrivals. There are both AC and fan rooms — specify the type when booking. Walk to Wat Phra That in the morning, about 10 minutes.

entries.storyHtml: BaanKong Hostel (formerly Baan Kong Homestay) is a small, new-building stay that's the cheapest in this guide from just ฿550, and owner-run, scoring 8.5 on Agoda from 12 reviews. It's in Lamphun town on Charoen Tha Road, about 2 km from Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the walking street — a short cycle or drive. Real guest reviews praise the cleanliness, the new building, a friendly owner who recommends places to go, a small front garden for breakfast, and bikes to rent for exploring the old town. The trade-off: it's small with few rooms, no hotel-style facilities, and the front desk keeps set hours. Best for budget travellers, couples, or road-trippers wanting a slow stop in Lamphun.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The desk keeps set hours, so tell the owner your arrival time ahead to avoid waiting. Rent a bike for a loop around Wat Phra That and the old city wall — ask the owner for routes. Some rooms catch road noise, so ask for one deeper from the road.

entries.storyHtml: Suksatan @ Lamphun is a boutique resort of Lanna-style wooden bungalows set across a leafy garden with a pond and a small waterfall — a quiet garden atmosphere that's rare at this price, scoring 8.5 from real reviews (Trip.com 8.4 · Tripadvisor 4.5/5) across 60 reviews. It's in Umong, about 5–6 km from the old town and Wat Phra That, with Chiang Mai 30–40 minutes' drive away. Real guest reviews praise the clean wooden rooms, private balconies (some bungalows sit over the pond), made-to-order breakfast, and an owner so kind it feels like staying with family. The trade-off: it's outside town and needs a car, a road and railway nearby bring intermittent noise, and it's a small resort with no pool. Best for couples and families with a car who want a quiet garden stay.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a bungalow over the pond or deeper in the garden — better views and quieter than those near the road. Bring or rent a car from Chiang Mai, since public transport in Lamphun is limited. Order a freshly cooked hot breakfast and eat it in the garden. Book ahead in the cool season, as it fills fast.

It's in Pa Sak, still within Mueang district, about an 8–10 minute drive into the city centre and 5 km from Wat Phra That. Real guest reviews praise the roomy rooms and bathrooms, fast-cooling AC, the handy in-room kitchenette for longer stays, and friendly staff. The trade-off: it's near a main road, so roadside rooms catch truck noise at night, there's no pool, and few restaurants nearby. Best for self-drivers staying several nights who prioritise value.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Roadside rooms catch traffic noise, so ask for a garden-facing inner room — much quieter. Use the in-room kitchenette to save on food, buying supplies at the Lamphun town market. Set GPS before you arrive to find the entrance easily.

entries.storyHtml: Maneenaksen Resort is the cheapest stay in this guide from just ฿500 — a Lanna-style garden resort of about 19 wooden and concrete houses set amid flower gardens, vegetable plots and jasmine-rice fields, scoring 7.4 from 16 reviews. It's in Pa Sang district south of the city, near Wat Phra Phutthabat Tak Pha, about 15–20 minutes from the old town. Real guest reviews praise the quiet, the greenery and the very low price; it also has a herbal steam room and an airport-transfer service that are rare at this price. To be honest, though, it's an older, simple property with ageing decor, no pool, an out-of-town location that needs a car, and it isn't on every big booking platform. Best for self-drivers after a rural escape on a tight budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pa Sang is awkward for public transport, so driving yourself is easiest — there's parking on site. It isn't on every big booking platform, so call or message the resort's Facebook to check availability and the latest price before you go. Stop at Wat Phra Phutthabat Tak Pha on the hill in the morning. Plan meals ahead, as restaurants nearby are few.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Lamphun hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in around Lamphun?
faq.a: It depends on your style and whether you have a car. The old town (around Wat Phra That Hariphunchai and the walking street) suits people who want to walk to temples and markets and don't have a car (Pickbaan, The First Residence, BaanKong). The Wiang Yong–Pa Sak fringe is where the hotels and resorts with pools, bigger rooms and free parking sit, near Jampha mall, best for self-drivers and families (Siri, GRAND PA, Look at Home, Huandalha). The outlying districts — Pa Sang, Ban Hong, Umong — are quiet garden stays at low prices that need a car (Maneenaksen, Loft House, Suksatan).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Lamphun hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary: budget stays and hostels start around ฿500–700/night (Maneenaksen, BaanKong, Loft House, Pickbaan, The Grand Jamjuree); mid-range hotels and resorts up to 4-star run about ฿800–1,050 (Look at Home, Suksatan, The First Residence, Huandalha, Nornlamphun, Siri, GRAND PA). All are approximate from-rates for standard rooms. During festivals and merit-making events at Wat Phra That, in-town rooms fill fast and rates climb.

faq.q: ❓ Is Lamphun easy to get around without a car?
faq.a: Honestly, Lamphun has no metro and is much harder for Grab than Chiang Mai, as drivers mostly work the Chiang Mai side. Without a car, stay in the old town where you can walk to Wat Phra That, the walking street and the markets — Pickbaan (walk to the temple), The First Residence (walk to the temple, near the station) or BaanKong (in town, with bikes to explore). Almost everything in Wiang Yong–Pa Sak and the outlying districts needs a car.

faq.q: ❓ Which Lamphun hotels have a pool and suit families?
faq.a: Pool stays in Lamphun aren't many. Look at Home Lamphun ฿800 has several pools and a separate shallow kids' pool, best for bringing children to swim. GRAND PA Hotel & Resort ฿1,050 has a big pool with a Pool Bar and a gym. The Grand Jamjuree Resort ฿700 is a lakeside resort with a pool and spa. Siri Hotel also has a small pool as a bonus.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay to walk to Wat Phra That Hariphunchai?
faq.a: Wat Phra That Hariphunchai is in the heart of the old town. The walkable stays are Pickbaan Hostel & Cafe ฿650, an old teak house in the old town within walking distance of the temple and walking street, and The First Residence Lamphun ฿800, a 0.6 km (~10-minute) walk from the temple, near the train station. BaanKong is in town about 2 km from the temple — a short cycle or drive.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking Lamphun hotels?
faq.a: Prices differ across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com depending on each site's promotions, so open and compare all three before booking — every review page in this guide includes the comparison links, which can save hundreds of baht a night. Some local stays such as Maneenaksen Resort aren't on every big booking platform, so you may need to contact the resort directly.
